question_text: A government cooperative deposited P100,000 in a bank that pays 4% simple interest per year. How much interest will it earn after 3 years?

hint_ladder.title: Orient yourself
hint_ladder.text: It's simple interest: interest earned only on the original principal each year, not on accumulated balance.

hint_ladder.title: The formula
hint_ladder.text: Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time. Rate as decimal: 4% = 0.04, time in years.

hint_ladder.title: Step 1: Yearly interest
hint_ladder.text: Yearly interest: P100,000 × 0.04 = P4,000. That's the amount per year.

hint_ladder.title: Final step
hint_ladder.text: Multiply yearly P4,000 by 3 years = P12,000 total interest.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you used 2 years instead of 3—multiply yearly P4,000 by 2 gives P8,000.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you used 2.5 years or misread the rate, giving P10,000.

C.text: Correct. P12,000 is the interest after 3 years.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you used 3.5 years instead of 3, calculating P14,000.

next_time_rule: Compute the yearly interest muna (Principal × Rate), then multiply by number of years. This avoids time period errors.
deconstruct_text:
Isipin mo, Barangay San Isidro’s cooperative deposits P100,000 in a rural bank for their livelihood program. 4% simple interest per year. That means interest is computed only on the original P100,000, hindi lumalaki. So each year, they earn P4,000.

Mental Trick: Kunin mo agad ang yearly na P4,000 (P100k x 4%). Para sa total, multiply lang sa years. Parang ipon: alam mo na monthly, times lang. Tandaan: ‘Yearly muna, saka multiply.’ Iwas maling taon.

**Watch-Out Zone: unit_conversion_trap** in action. Time slip? Compute annual interest ...
